name: Tetouan Kasbah
hero_subtitle: Quiet imperial landmark in Tetouan — controlled access, fine craft and a calmer tone than the square.

info.entry_val: Rules vary — check on the day

overview.title: Where the sultan's memory is kept
overview.p1: The Tetouan Kasbah holds the memorial of the sultan who made Tetouan an imperial capital. The complex mixes quiet courtyards with fine zellige, plaster and woodwork — a formal, reflective stop away from the busy square.
overview.p2: Access rules can change and some areas may be restricted. Dress modestly, follow staff guidance, and treat the visit as an official stop rather than a photo outing. Time inside is usually short but intense.
overview.p3: Come in the morning when queues are lighter. Pair it with other Tetouan landmarks the same day so the imperial story — power, logistics and memory — stays connected.

food.title: Eat before or after — not inside
food.p1: There is no dining inside the memorial. Plan tea on the main square beforehand or lunch in the medina later.

tips.title: Practical tips for the Tetouan Kasbah

1.title: Check access before planning the morning
1.desc: Opening hours and rules can change. Confirm in the morning with your hotel or at the entrance so you do not build the whole plan on a closed section.

2.title: Dress and behaviour matter here
2.desc: This is a memorial place. Speak quietly, dress modestly, and put the camera away when staff ask. A short respectful visit is better than an argument at the door.

3.title: Link it with other Tetouan sites
3.desc: The kasbah and other imperial stops tell connected stories. Visiting them the same morning keeps transport simple and the history clear.

q1.question: Can non-Muslims visit?
q1.answer: Access policies have varied over time. Check on the day, respect restricted zones, and follow staff instructions without debate.

q2.question: Is there a dress code?
q2.answer: Yes — modest clothing covering shoulders and knees is expected. Bring a scarf if you are unsure.

q3.question: How long is the visit?
q3.answer: Twenty to forty minutes is typical once you are inside the open areas.

q4.question: Is photography allowed?
q4.answer: Rules differ by room. Ask before you shoot and avoid flash in sensitive spaces.

q5.question: Best time to come?
q5.answer: Morning, soon after opening, for fewer groups and cooler air.
